name: Expat
baseline: libxml2 SAX parser (xmlSAXUserParseMemory with no-op handlers); also Xerces-C++ SAX
workload: Parse-only SAX run with no-op start, end and character handlers over generated xmlgen documents (4 KB, 256 KB, 32 MB), an OPC-DA message generator (3.5 KB x 80000 messages and 3 MB x 100 messages) and a 12 MB DMOZ RDF dump, Expat against libxml2 SAX and Xerces-C++ SAX in the xmlbench suite.
claimed_speedup: Parsing time, lower is better, from sample.results/08.02.2004/sample.res. Expat vs libxml2 SAX: 4 KB 0.132 vs 0.159 ms; 256 KB 9.062 vs 9.798 ms; 32 MB 1129.735 vs 1285.889 ms; 3.5 KB x 80000 9857.613 vs 12198.505 ms; 3 MB x 100 11902.892 vs 13700.148 ms; DMOZ 12 MB 294.210 vs 432.529 ms (1.08x to 1.47x faster, derived from page data). Expat vs Xerces-C++ SAX: 32 MB 1129.735 vs 2551.442 ms; DMOZ 12 MB 294.210 vs 969.123 ms (2.3x to 3.3x faster across all six workloads, derived from page data). Expat SAX vs libxml2 native tree build (not like-for-like): 3.2x to 4.9x (derived).
compiler_and_flags: gcc 3.3.1 or 2.96 (stated in the result header); optimisation flags not stated; the repo's parse/Makefile appends only -g and Makefile.in sets FLAGS empty; the library builds under test are not described
tradeoffs: Non-validating, stream-oriented push parser in C99 with no tree, so the caller builds any document structure; libxml2 adds DOM, validation, XPath, XInclude and HTML parsing. The Expat README and Changes carry a notice that Expat has unfixed security issues (issue #1160), and the 2.x line has had several quadratic-runtime CVE fixes.
caveats: Old and contradicted by newer data, so low confidence. (1) The numbers are a 2004 snapshot of xmlbench 1.3.0 (author in AUTHORS file; GPL benchmark code) that the originjs/libxml-benchmark repo imported in 2024; the README lists tested version ranges only (Expat 1.95.5-1.95.6, libxml2 2.4.30-2.6.5, Xerces-C 2.1-2.4), not the versions behind this run, and all are 20 years older than Expat 2.9.0. (2) The repo's current driver sources were edited by the importer (Chinese comments, is_sax_parser field, XML_ParserReset in expat.c), so they may differ from the 2004 drivers; libxml-sax.c leaves startElementNs and endElementNs NULL under XML_SAX2_MAGIC when LIBXML_VERSION > 20600, which can make libxml2 skip callbacks and favours libxml2 if anything. (3) Optimisation flags are not stated. (4) A current third-party run of the same kind of task points the other way: bemayer/xml-benchmark gh-pages report (generated 2026-10-01, ubuntu-latest GitHub Actions, no CPU or library versions or flags stated, 1 star) has libxml2 SAX/Stream faster than Expat at every size, for example 1 MB 4.975 vs 39.008 ms, 10 MB 18.833 vs 69.255 ms, 100 MB 167.821 vs 431.529 ms; the same run has Expat ahead of Xerces (Java) at 1 KB to 1 MB but behind at 10 MB (69.255 vs 63.145 ms) and 100 MB (431.529 vs 344.143 ms). An earlier committed snapshot of that report (2026-04-06, local runner) also has libxml2 ahead. Those libxml2 throughputs (up to 6622 MB/s) look implausible for equal work, which was not investigated. (5) Another seed record for the same repo exists in data/wave4/raw/w4-mine-a.json (tier C, libsimdxml README, Expat SAX vs libxml2 DOM); this one should replace or merge with it, and it needs a shared paper id before merge. (6) Expat's own README and docs carry no benchmark numbers; pugixml.org/benchmark and the 2007 gnome and expat-discuss threads were blocked here and not read.
